patch.value: Install the pinned release npm into a job-local prefix

The release workflow replaces the runner's global npm with the pinned npm. Parallel jobs on one runner host share the toolcache Node installation, so one job's global install mutates a sibling job's npm mid-install (ENOTEMPTY, or npm: command not found), as reported by unbraind/pm-ops#284 for the fleet.

The release workflow installs the pinned npm with --prefix into a job-local directory and prepends that prefix bin to the job path; The workflow keeps the exact-version assertion on the effective npm; A workflow-contract test fails if any workflow replaces the global npm

value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Root cause (fleet-wide, reported as unbraind/pm-ops#284): after setup-node, every deep and release job ran a global npm install of the pinned npm. On the shared local runners, all containers on one host share the toolcache Node installation mounted at the runner tool directory, so parallel jobs replaced the same npm and siblings failed with ENOTEMPTY (exit 217) or npm: command not found (exit 127). Fix: the release workflow installs the pinned npm into a job-local prefix and prepends that prefix bin to the job path, keeping the exact-version assertion on the effective npm. Contract updates: the pinned-bootstrap step assertions require the prefix form, only the install step itself may prepend to the job path, and a new workflow-wide audit fails if any workflow replaces the global npm. Gates: typecheck, the full quick tier (1028 tests) and changelog:check all pass on this branch.

Round AF follow-up on the fail-closed guard, from the pm-ado review threads PRRT_kwDOUMUq1864PGRG and PRRT_kwDOUMUq1864P73_ and the identical pm-lint threads PRRT_kwDOVHTnEc64QBn2, PRRT_kwDOVHTnEc64QBn6 and PRRT_kwDOVHTnEc64QBn7; this repository carries the same guard with the direct YAML dependency. All three findings were reproduced against the guard source first: a prefix bootstrap followed by '&& npm install -g npm@11.19.0', 'npm install -gpld npm@11.19.0' and step env NPM_CONFIG_GLOBAL=true were all accepted by the previous code.

1. Segment-scoped prefix exception: run scripts now split into command segments at unquoted ;, &, | and newlines. The scanner tracks quote state across lines and $( … ) substitutions (which nest a fresh quoting context even inside double quotes), skips comments and here-document bodies, and any script that cannot be delimited (unbalanced quote or substitution) fails closed as 'undelimitable command line'. The job-local prefix exception only covers the segment carrying it; rejected fixtures add 'npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/npm-11.19.0" npm@11.19.0 && npm install -g npm@11.19.0' and 'npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/npm-local" npm@11.19.0; npm install -g npm@11.19.0'. Approved bootstrap fixtures stay accepted.
2. Combined short flags: any single-dash letter cluster containing g now marks global (rejected: 'npm install -gpld npm@11.19.0', 'npm install -dg npm@11.19.0'); 'npm install -D pnpm' and 'npm install -gpld pnpm' stay accepted.
3. Workflow, job and step env compose for each step run, the step scope taking precedence; npm reads npm_config_* keys case-insensitively. npm_config_global set to anything other than false/0/empty, npm_config_location=global, a ${{ … }} expression value, or an unreadable env scope or entry forces every npm install in that run global unless its own segment carries a job-local prefix. Fixtures cover step env flow mapping, job env flow and block styles, workflow env, expression values, location=global, step-override (job "true" + step "false" accepted) and accepted "false"/"0"/"" values.
